title: Learn2Play Bench: How Well Do LLM Agents Learn from Experience in Unfamiliar Environments?
title_zh: Learn2Play benchmark: Evaluation of LLM agents' ability to learn effectively in unfamiliar environments through novel rule-based text games.

paragraphs.en: Learning from experience is essential for LLM agents to adapt to unfamiliar and dynamic environments. Evaluating this ability is therefore important for understanding how effectively agents acquire and use new knowledge. Existing benchmarks have sought to evaluate this ability, but they primarily evaluate tasks whose rules are provided in the instructions or already familiar to pretrained models, making it difficult to distinguish learning from interactions from reasoning with existing knowledge. To address this, we introduce Learn2Play Bench , a benchmark of newly designed text-based games, whose rules are novel or counterintuitive, requiring agents to acquire knowledge through interaction rather than rely solely on pretrained knowledge. These games provide reproducible feedback and automatic scoring, enabling controlled evaluation of learning across repeated attempts. We also vary game instances to test whether agents can apply what they have learned to new situations. Therefore, we evaluate how backbone models, self-evolving methods, and agent harnesses affect agents’ learning ability, revealing three findings: (1) Experience retention: Retaining complete records of actions and feedback can support more effective learning than summarizing these experiences into rules or strategies. (2) Human–agent gap: Top-performing human players achieve higher peak scores than the evaluated agents. Humans explore more varied strategies, and repeat actions less. (3) Harness matters: With the backbone fixed, changing the harness can improve performance while reducing estimated inference cost. Together, these findings provide insights into how LLM agents learn from experience and suggest directions for future work to improve their learning ability. Project website: https://liushiliushi.github.io/learn2play-bench-website/ .

paragraphs.en: The ability of LLM agents to acquire new knowledge through interaction and use it to improve behavior is central to artificial general intelligence (AGI) ( Hendrycks et al., 2025 ) . While the extensive knowledge acquired during pretraining enables agents to perform complex tasks (e.g., fixing software issues ( Yang et al., 2024 ) , completing web tasks ( Zhou et al., 2024 ) , and operating desktop applications ( Xie et al., 2024 ) ), in realistic deployment, agents often encounter unfamiliar environments whose rules are not covered by the pretrained knowledge. For example, an agent struggles to control a robot through an unfamiliar command interface. It must therefore try commands and observe the resulting motion to learn which joints each command activates. Agents can then apply what they have learned to make better decisions in subsequent interactions.
paragraphs.zh: LLM 智能体通过互动获取新知识并利用这些知识改进行为的能力，是通用人工智能（AGI）的核心（Hendrycks 等，2025）。 尽管预训练期间获得的广泛知识使智能体能够执行复杂任务（例如，修复软件问题（Yang 等，2024）、完成网页任务（Zhou 等，2024）以及操作桌面应用程序（Xie 等，2024）），但在实际部署中，智能体常常会遇到其规则未被预训练知识涵盖的不熟悉环境。 例如，一个智能体难以通过不熟悉的命令接口控制机器人。 因此，它必须尝试各种命令并观察产生的运动，以学习每个命令会激活哪些关节。 随后，智能体可以将所学知识应用于后续互动中，从而做出更优决策。

paragraphs.en: Recent work has therefore developed self-evolving agents that reuse interaction feedback through memories, extracted rules, reasoning patterns, or evolving agent configurations ( Zhang et al., 2025b ; He et al., 2025 ; Ouyang et al., 2025 ) . However, evaluating whether these systems actually learn remains difficult. Existing methods are often studied with different models, tasks, and evaluation protocols, making their learning behavior hard to compare directly. More fundamentally, better task performance does not necessarily mean that an agent learns more effectively . If an agent improves on a familiar task, we do not know whether it learned a new rule from interaction or merely recovered knowledge already encoded during pretraining.

paragraphs.en: How effectively can LLM agents learn from experience in unfamiliar environments?

paragraphs.en: To answer this question, we introduce Learn2Play Bench , a benchmark of newly designed text-based games with unfamiliar or counterintuitive hidden rules. For example, in one game, stealing a colleague’s lunch helps the player get promoted, while working hard does not. Agents are not given these rules. They must discover them by acting, observing textual feedback, and carrying useful experience into later episodes, without updating model weights. Each game provides deterministic feedback and automatic scoring, allowing learning trajectories to be measured reproducibly. In half of the games, characters, objects, or layouts change across episodes while the underlying rules remain fixed. This setting tests whether agents can apply knowledge to new situations.

paragraphs.en: Using this controlled setting, we compare different backbone models, self-evolving methods, and deployed agent harnesses, and contrast their behavior with human players. Our experiments reveal five main findings: (1) Preserving evidence can matter more than compressing it. Raw interaction histories can support stronger learning than methods that summarize experience into rules or strategies, because the original evidence remains available when earlier conclusions need revision (§4.2). (2) Top-performing human players outperform the best agent. Top-performing human players reach higher peak scores than the evaluated agents, while exploring more varied action sequences and recovering more often after setbacks (§4.4). (3) Better harnesses can improve agent performance and learning while reducing inference cost. With the backbone fixed, changing the harness can substantially improve both performance and learning. In some cases, it also reduces inference cost through fewer model calls and less repeated context (§4.3, §4.6). (4) Agents can learn more slowly in changing environments , even when the underlying rules stay the same. The drop in learning slope tends to be larger for weaker backbones under the same harness (§4.5). (5) Agents can learn rules from experience but still struggle to use them to develop effective strategies. For example, in Haunted Inn , an agent learns how to assign guests to safe rooms but fails to plan ahead, leaving a later guest with nowhere safe to stay (§4.2).
paragraphs.zh: 在这种受控设置中，我们比较了不同的骨干模型、自我演化方法以及部署的智能体框架，并将其行为与人类玩家的表现进行了对比。 我们的实验揭示了五个主要发现：（1）保留证据可能比压缩证据更为重要。 原始交互历史能够支持比那些将经验总结为规则或策略的方法更强的学习能力，因为当早期结论需要修正时，原始证据仍然可用（§4.2）。 （2）表现最佳的人类玩家优于最出色的智能体。 表现最佳的人类玩家能够达到比受评估智能体更高的峰值分数，同时探索更多样化的行动序列，并在遭遇挫折后更频繁地恢复过来（§4.4）。 （3）更优的智能体框架可以在降低推理成本的同时提升智能体的性能和学习能力。 在骨干模型固定的情况下，改变智能体框架可以显著提升性能和学习能力。 在某些情况下，它还能通过减少模型调用和重复上下文来降低推理成本（§4.3、§4.6）。 （4）在变化的环境中，即使底层规则保持不变，智能体的学习速度也可能变慢。 在相同框架下，较弱的骨干模型其学习斜率下降的趋势通常更明显（§4.5）。 （5）智能体虽然能够从经验中学习规则，但仍难以利用这些规则制定有效的策略。 例如，在《Haunted Inn》中，一个智能体学会了如何将客人分配到安全的房间，但却无法提前规划，导致后来的客人没有安全的地方可住（§4.2）。

paragraphs.en: Self-evolving agents. Recent work develops self-evolving agents to learn from experience at test time, adapting their behavior using feedback from earlier attempts. Early methods reuse experience without updating model weights through verbal reflections in Reflexion ( Shinn et al., 2023 ) , extracted insights and retrieved trajectories in ExpeL ( Zhao et al., 2024 ) , or reusable executable skills in Voyager ( Wang et al., 2024 ) . Other methods organize experience into workflows and playbooks. For example, AWM induces action workflows ( Wang et al., 2025 ) , Dynamic Cheatsheet curates compact strategies and code snippets ( Suzgun et al., 2026 ) , and ACE incrementally maintains structured playbooks rather than raw transcripts ( Zhang et al., 2025b ) . ReasoningBank and ERL distill trajectories into reusable reasoning patterns or heuristics ( Ouyang et al., 2025 ; Allard et al., 2026 ) . Beyond constructing memories, GEPA evolves prompts through trajectory-level reflection ( Agrawal et al., 2025 ) , while Agents of Change revises both prompts and agent code through specialized collaborative roles ( Belle et al., 2025 ) . EvoTest extends evolution to the broader agent configuration, including memory and tool-use routines ( He et al., 2025 ) . Meta-TTL further evolves the adaptation policy that determines how experience should update the agent ( Lou et al., 2026 ) . Beyond context-level updates, TT-SI generates training examples from uncertain cases and fine-tunes the agent at test time ( Acikgoz et al., 2026 ) . Our goal is not to propose another adaptation method, but to assess how effectively existing methods learn under controlled conditions. Our evaluation focuses on learning without weight updates: we compare backbones in a common harness and self-evolving methods with each backbone held fixed.
paragraphs.zh: 自我演化的智能体。 近期的研究开发了能够于测试时从经验中学习的自我演化智能体，这些智能体利用早期尝试的反馈来调整自身行为。 早期的方法通过 Reflexion（Shinn 等人，2023）中的语言反思、ExpeL（Zhao 等人，2024）中提取的洞察与检索的轨迹，或 Voyager（Wang 等人，2024）中可重复使用的可执行技能，在无需更新模型权重的情况下复用经验。 其他方法则将经验组织为工作流和剧本。 例如，AWM 会生成动作工作流（Wang 等人，2025），Dynamic Cheatsheet 会整理出简洁的策略和代码片段（Suzgun 等人，2026），而 ACE 则会逐步维护结构化的剧本，而非原始转录文本（Zhang 等人，2025b）。 ReasoningBank 和 ERL 将轨迹提炼为可重复使用的推理模式或启发式规则（Ouyang 等人，2025；Allard 等人，2026）。 除了构建记忆外，GEPA 还通过轨迹层面的反思来演化提示（Agrawal 等人，2025），而 Agents of Change 则通过专门的协作角色同时修订提示和智能体代码（Belle 等人，2025）。 EvoTest 将演化扩展至更广泛的智能体配置，包括记忆和工具使用流程（He 等人，2025）。 Meta-TTL 进一步演化决定经验如何更新智能体的适应策略（Lou 等人，2026）。 除了上下文层面的更新外，TT-SI 还会从不确定案例中生成训练样本，并在测试时对智能体进行微调（Acikgoz 等人，2026）。 我们的目标并非提出另一种适应方法，而是评估现有方法在受控条件下学习的效率。 我们的评估聚焦于无需更新权重的学习：我们在一个通用框架中比较不同的基础模型，并分别固定每个基础模型来测试自我演化方法的表现。

paragraphs.en: Benchmarks for self-evolving agents. To assess whether these adaptation mechanisms improve later behavior, benchmarks evaluate agents over task sequences or repeated interactions. StreamBench uses input–feedback streams ( Wu et al., 2024 ) , while MemoryBench studies learning from accumulated user feedback and Evo-Memory evaluates memory updates across task streams ( Ai et al., 2025 ; Wei et al., 2025 ) . Related evaluations extend experience reuse to interactive tasks: LifelongAgentBench tests skill accumulation across related tasks ( Zheng et al., 2025 ) , SWE-Bench-CL evaluates learning across successive coding issues ( Joshi et al., 2025 ) , and MemoryArena tests memory use across interdependent sessions ( He et al., 2026 ) . These benchmarks test whether experience improves later performance. On familiar tasks, however, it is unclear whether agents improve by learning something new or by using what they already know. Other benchmarks study learning directly through interaction with environments. AutoEnv ( Zhang et al., 2025a ) also creates new environments to evaluate learning across diverse settings. Closer to our setting, J-TTL ( He et al., 2025 ) measures repeated improvement on Jericho games, but their public content may already be represented in model pretraining. ARC-AGI-3 tests interaction with unfamiliar visual environments, but performance also depends on visual capabilities ( Foundation, 2026 ) . We use newly designed text-based games with hidden rules to examine whether agents can discover previously unknown rules through actions and feedback. We also compare fixed and changing instances of the same game to test whether agents can reuse experience when the visible situation changes.

paragraphs.en: To measure whether agents improve through experience in unfamiliar environments, we design games that satisfy the following principles:
paragraphs.zh: 为了衡量智能体是否能在不熟悉的环境中通过经验获得提升，我们设计了满足以下原则的游戏：

paragraphs.en: Rule novelty. We design games with novel hidden rules not found in existing games, including deliberately counterintuitive rules that conflict with common game knowledge. For example, in one of our games, instead of hard work, stealing a colleague’s lunch helps the player get promoted. The agent must therefore learn which actions lead to promotion from the game’s feedback, rather than rely on expectations about real workplaces.
paragraphs.zh: 规则新颖性。 我们设计的游戏包含现有游戏中从未出现过的全新隐藏规则，其中还包括故意设置的反直觉规则，这些规则与常见的游戏知识相冲突。 例如，在我们的一款游戏中，玩家并非通过努力工作晋升，而是通过偷走同事的午餐来实现晋升。 因此，智能体必须根据游戏中的反馈来学习哪些行为能带来晋升，而不是依赖对现实工作场所的预期。

paragraphs.en: Based on the four principles above, we manually design Learn2Play Bench with 20 game templates, each of which can generate multiple instances that differ in layout, characters, or hidden-rule parameters. Figure 1 illustrates the game suite and an example interaction. Agents receive a goal and a set of available actions, interact through text to discover the hidden rules, and receive a final score at the end of each episode. They play repeated episodes and can use experience from earlier attempts. We divide the games along two dimensions. First, ten fixed games repeat the same instance across episodes, whereas ten re-shuffled games change the visible instance while preserving the core rule. Second, we conduct pilot evaluations with several agents to estimate game difficulty and identify five challenge games. 1 1 1 The challenge games are Catnip , DreamGarden , Mola Tea , RedEye , and Roadside Observatory . We use a ten-episode scoring window for these games and a five-episode window for the remaining normal games. Appendix A explains what players must learn in each game, and appendix D provides the corresponding results and archived rule-discovery evidence.

paragraphs.en: Baseline models. To examine how learning from experience varies across different backbones, we compare nine models using OpenCode ( OpenCode Contributors, 2026 ) , an open-source coding agent harness that connects configurable language models to shell and file tools. We use its command-line agent as a common harness for black-box game interaction through the replay interface, keeping the agent loop, prompts, replay protocol, and memory format fixed across backbones. The backbones are Claude Opus 5, Claude Sonnet 5, Gemini 3.5 Flash, Gemini 3.7 Flash, GPT-5.6-SOL, GPT-5 Mini, DeepSeek V4 Pro, Kimi K3, and Qwen 3.8 Max.

paragraphs.en: Methods. To examine how different ways of retaining and reusing experience affect learning, we compare self-evolving methods separately for Kimi K3, Claude Opus 5, and GPT-5 Mini, holding the backbone fixed within each comparison. We evaluate the following methods: Naive retains the dialogue within the current episode but discards it before the next, providing no cross-episode experience. Memory cumulatively adds the complete, unmodified interaction histories from preceding episodes to each new episode’s prompt, dropping the oldest episodes only when the history exceeds the context budget. Reflexion ( Shinn et al., 2023 ) reflects on each completed episode to derive concise lessons about discovered rules, successful and failed actions, and next steps, then adds the accumulated lessons to the prompt for later episodes. EvoTest ( He et al., 2025 ) uses earlier interaction histories and outcomes to evolve a guiding prompt and a state-extraction program that steer action selection in subsequent episodes. ReasoningBank ( Ouyang et al., 2025 ) turns each successful or failed episode into a small set of reusable reasoning lessons and adds the accumulated bank to the prompt in later episodes. Agent Workflow Memory (AWM) ( Wang et al., 2025 ) induces reusable multi-step workflows from successful interaction histories and includes the resulting workflows in later episode prompts. Failed episodes are not used.

paragraphs.en: Stronger models use feedback to adjust their decisions, whereas weaker models may repeat the same actions despite new observations. We inspected the interaction logs to understand how models use experience. Opus 5 and Qwen 3.8 Max test their understanding of the hidden rules and update it when new observations do not match their expectations. In contrast, weaker models sometimes repeat actions that worked before, even when they no longer work. They may also change several factors at once, making it hard to tell which factor affects the outcome. For example, in Poisoner , agents choose dishes for a king and learn about his food preferences from whether he accepts or rejects them. In one GPT-5 Mini run, the agent keeps choosing dishes by their position on the menu, without using feedback from earlier choices. Kimi K3 instead uses that feedback to choose which food attribute to test next.
paragraphs.zh: 更强的模型会利用反馈来调整其决策，而较弱的模型即使面对新的观察结果，也可能重复执行相同的操作。 我们检查了交互日志，以了解模型如何利用经验。 Opus 5 和 Qwen 3.8 Max 会测试它们对隐藏规则的理解，并在新的观察结果与预期不符时更新这种理解。 相比之下，较弱的模型有时会重复之前有效但现在已不再奏效的操作。 它们也可能同时改变多个因素，这使得难以判断究竟是哪个因素影响了结果。 例如，在《Poisoner》中，智能体为国王选择菜肴，并通过国王接受或拒绝这些菜肴来了解他的饮食偏好。 在一次 GPT-5 Mini 的运行中，该智能体持续根据菜肴在菜单上的位置进行选择，并未利用早期选择带来的反馈。 而 Kimi K3 则会利用这种反馈来决定接下来要测试哪种食物属性。

paragraphs.en: Simply using past interaction histories can outperform more elaborate self-evolving methods. Memory retains raw histories without reflection, rule extraction, or workflow induction, yet leads all four metrics with Kimi K3. This is because reflection and memory processing can turn an incomplete understanding into rules or workflows that later episodes continue to follow, while raw histories keep the original evidence available for revising those interpretations. For example, in GemForge , agents combine ingredients to make gems. After one combination fails, an EvoTest–Opus 5 run adds a rule to its prompt telling it to avoid many other combinations, including one that would succeed.
paragraphs.zh: 仅使用过往的交互历史，其表现就可能优于更复杂的自我演化方法。 记忆仅保留原始的历史记录，没有进行反思、规则提取或工作流程推导，但它在所有四项指标中均优于 Kimi K3。 这是因为反思和记忆处理能够将不完整的理解转化为规则或工作流程，后续的流程会持续遵循这些规则；而原始历史记录则保留了最初的证据，可用于修正这些解释。 例如，在 GemForge 中，智能体通过组合各种成分来制造宝石。 在一次组合失败后，EvoTest–Opus 5 的运行会在其提示中添加一条规则，要求它避免许多其他组合，包括一个本可以成功的组合。

paragraphs.en: OpenCode achieves better performance than the evaluated self-evolving methods when using the same backbone. OpenCode is more flexible during play. OpenCode lets the model decide when to review earlier feedback, run calculations, or check a plan before taking an action. By contrast, the evaluated self-evolving methods follow preset steps for choosing actions and updating experience. When an unexpected result occurs, OpenCode gives the model room to investigate and revise its plan before continuing, rather than only updating its memory for later episodes.
paragraphs.zh: 在采用相同主干模型时，OpenCode 的表现优于所评估的自演化方法。 OpenCode 在游戏过程中更具灵活性。 OpenCode 允许模型自行决定何时回顾早期反馈、执行计算或在采取行动前检查计划。 相比之下，所评估的自演化方法遵循预设的步骤来选择行动和更新经验。 当出现意外结果时，OpenCode 会给予模型在继续之前进行调查和修订计划的空间，而不仅仅是为后续回合更新记忆。

paragraphs.en: Human Top-1 achieves higher Max than the models and self-evolving methods evaluated in our experiments. This may be because humans explore more broadly, whereas agents exploit discovered strategies more consistently. To examine this behavioral difference beyond the single best record, we compare observed episodes from Human Top-3 with the models and self-evolving methods. In fixed games, consecutive action sequences have an average similarity of 0.54 for humans and 0.66 for agents. After a lower-scoring episode, humans reach a new personal best in the next episode 33% of the time, compared with 22% for agents. These observations suggest that humans more often change strategies and recover from temporary failures, while agents more often repeat a reliable but potentially suboptimal strategy.
paragraphs.zh: 人类 Top-1 实现的 Max 值高于我们实验中评估的模型和自演化方法。 这可能是因为人类探索的范围更广，而智能体则更稳定地利用已发现的策略。 为了在单一最佳记录之外考察这种行为差异，我们将人类 Top-3 的观察到的回合与模型和自演化方法进行比较。 在固定游戏中，连续动作序列的平均相似度对人类为 0.54，对智能体为 0.66。 在得分较低的回合之后，人类有 33% 的概率在下一回合达到新的个人最佳成绩，而智能体为 22%。 这些观察结果表明，人类更频繁地改变策略并从暂时失败中恢复，而智能体则更频繁地重复一种可靠但可能非最优的策略。

paragraphs.en: With the model fixed, a better-suited harness can improve performance while reducing cost. OpenCode with Kimi K3 achieves higher Max at lower estimated cost than Memory , EvoTest, and ReasoningBank. Claude Code with Opus 5 also outperforms these self-evolving methods and OpenCode at lower estimated cost. For Kimi K3, OpenCode uses 56% fewer input tokens than Memory and 71% and 41% fewer generated tokens than EvoTest and ReasoningBank, respectively, as reported in Table 11 . These self-evolving methods call the model for each action and repeatedly supply past interactions or stored memories. OpenCode instead executes several actions from one model response and removes repeated game feedback, reducing model calls and repeated input.
paragraphs.zh: 在模型固定的情况下，更合适的约束机制可以在降低成本的同时提升性能。 与 Memory、EvoTest 和 ReasoningBank 相比，使用 Kimi K3 的 OpenCode 在预估成本更低的情况下实现了更高的 Max。 使用 Opus 5 的 Claude Code 也在预估成本更低的情况下超越了这些自我演化方法以及 OpenCode。 如表 11 所示，对于 Kimi K3，OpenCode 使用的输入标记比 Memory 少 56%，生成的标记也比 EvoTest 和 ReasoningBank 分别少 71% 和 41%。 这些自我演化方法会在每次操作时调用模型，并重复提供过往的交互记录或存储的记忆。 相比之下，OpenCode 会基于单次模型响应执行多个操作，并移除重复的游戏反馈，从而减少模型调用和重复输入。

paragraphs.en: Building on our findings, we discuss open questions in how to improve the learning ability of LLM agents and outline directions for future research.
paragraphs.zh: 基于我们的研究结果，我们将探讨如何提升大型语言模型智能体的学习能力这一领域中的开放性问题，并概述未来研究的可行方向。

paragraphs.en: How should agents balance exploration and exploitation? In our comparison of human players and agents, Human Top-1 achieves a higher Max score than every agent configuration we evaluate, as shown in Tables 2 and 4.3 . This is because humans try more varied strategies across episodes, while agents more often reuse strategies that have worked before (Appendix B.3.3 ). Future work should better balance exploration and exploitation, allowing agents to test new strategies even when their current strategy already earns high scores.
paragraphs.zh: 智能体应如何平衡探索与利用？ 在人类玩家与智能体的对比中，如表 2 和 4.3 所示，Human Top-1 实现的 Max 分数高于我们评估的所有智能体配置。 这是因为人类会在不同回合尝试更多样化的策略，而智能体则更倾向于重复使用之前奏效的策略（附录 B.3.3）。 未来的研究应更好地平衡探索与利用，使智能体即使在当前策略已能获得高分时，也能测试新的策略。

sents.en: Future work should better balance exploration and exploitation, allowing agents to test new strategies even when their current strategy already earns high scores.

paragraphs.en: How should agents store learned rules? With Kimi K3, Memory outperforms the other self-evolving methods overall, as shown in Table 2 . Unlike those methods, it retains full interaction histories rather than first distilling them into rules. This distinction matters when agents draw rules from limited evidence. In GemForge , EvoTest tried one gem combination and failed, but its later prompt instructed the agent not to test other combinations it had never tried (Appendix B.1.3 ). The prompt thus turned incomplete evidence into a definitive rule. Future work can explore ways to store experience, such as linking each learned rule to the original interactions behind it so agents can revisit the evidence and revise the rule when new feedback arrives.
paragraphs.zh: 智能体应如何存储已学习的规则？ 如表 2 所示，在 Kimi K3 中，Memory 的整体表现优于其他自我演化方法。 与那些方法不同，它保留完整的交互历史，而不是先将它们提炼为规则。 当智能体从有限的证据中推导规则时，这种区别就显得尤为重要。 在 GemForge 中，EvoTest 尝试了一种宝石组合并失败了，但其后续的提示词指示智能体不要测试其他从未尝试过的组合（附录 B.1.3）。 因此，该提示词将不完整的证据转化为一条确定的规则。 未来的研究可以探索存储经验的方法，例如将每条已学习的规则与其背后的原始交互关联起来，这样当新反馈出现时，智能体就能重新审视证据并修正规则。

paragraphs.en: How can agents learn what stays constant as environments change? Our transfer evaluation shows that changing surface details, such as layouts or characters, can reduce agents’ learning slopes even when the underlying rules remain the same (Table 4.5 ). In real-world tasks, agents also regularly encounter changes in their surroundings, available resources, and the people they interact with. This raises a broader question: how can agents adapt to these changes in their environments? Future methods could help agents compare experiences across different situations, distinguish shared rules from instance-specific details, and check when those rules still apply.
paragraphs.zh: 智能体如何能够学会在环境变化时哪些因素保持不变？ 我们的迁移评估表明，改变表面细节（例如布局或角色）会降低智能体的学习斜率，即使底层规则保持不变（表 4.5）。 在实际任务中，智能体也会经常遇到周围环境、可用资源以及互动对象的变化。 这引出了一个更广泛的问题：智能体如何能够适应这些环境变化？ 未来的方法可以帮助智能体在不同情境下比较经验，区分通用规则与特定实例的细节，并判断这些规则是否仍然适用。

paragraphs.en: In this study, we investigate how effectively LLM agents learn from experience in unfamiliar environments. Existing evaluations make it difficult to distinguish newly acquired knowledge from prior knowledge. To address this issue, we introduce Learn2Play Bench, a benchmark of newly designed text-based games with hidden rules that agents discover through interaction without updating their model weights. We conducted comprehensive experiments comparing backbone models, self-evolving methods, deployed agent harnesses, and human players. Our findings show that more elaborate self-evolving methods do not always improve learning, human players explore more varied strategies, with top-performing humans achieving higher peak scores than the models and self-evolving methods we evaluate, and agent harnesses can improve performance while reducing task costs. We hope this work provides a foundation for evaluating and improving how agents learn from experience.
paragraphs.zh: 在本研究中，我们探讨了大型语言模型智能体在陌生环境中如何有效地从经验中学习。 现有的评估方法难以区分新获得的知识与先验知识。 为解决这一问题，我们提出了 Learn2Play Bench——一个基准测试平台，包含一系列新设计的文本类游戏，这些游戏具有隐藏规则，智能体无需更新模型权重，仅通过互动即可发现这些规则。 我们进行了全面的实验，对比了基础模型、自我演化方法、部署的智能体框架以及人类玩家的表现。 研究结果表明：更复杂的自我演化方法并不总能提升学习效果；人类玩家会探索更多样化的策略，其中表现最佳的人类玩家的峰值得分高于我们所评估的模型和自我演化方法；而智能体框架则能在提升性能的同时降低任务成本。 我们希望这项工作能为评估和改进智能体从经验中学习的方式提供基础。

paragraphs.en: Knowing taboos without reserving rooms. OpenCode–Opus 5 trial 1 records both the actor–scholar adjacency taboo and the mirror-room restriction on lantern carriers. Greedy placement leaves no safe room for the last actor. The agent then says “I need to reserve buffer positions proactively” and changes its allocation plan. The scores are 100 and 115, but the guest lists also change: the evidence is the revised allocation policy, not a controlled score improvement.
paragraphs.zh: 知晓禁忌却未预订房间。 OpenCode–Opus 5 试验 1 记录了演员与学者相邻的禁忌，以及灯笼携带者面临的镜像房间限制。 贪心式放置导致最后一个演员没有安全的房间可用。 智能体随后表示：“我需要主动预留缓冲位置”，并调整了分配计划。 得分分别为 100 和 115，但嘉宾名单也发生了变化：证据是修订后的分配策略，而非受控的得分提升。

paragraphs.en: One failed fusion becomes a broad rule. EvoTest–Opus 5 trial 3 scores 46, 81, 83, 83, and 83 in GemForge’s scoring window. An earlier prompt records that the only fusion tried, jade with opal, produced slag. The episode-5 prompt then instructs the agent never to attempt tier-2 or tier-3 fusion, ruling out combinations it has not tested. This case shows how a processed prompt can generalize beyond the observed failure. It does not establish that compression causes the aggregate difference from Memory.
paragraphs.zh: 一次失败的融合便成为一条普遍规则。 EvoTest–Opus 5 第 3 次试验在 GemForge 的评分窗口中获得了 46、81、83、83 和 83 的分数。 更早的一次提示记录显示，唯一尝试过的融合——玉与欧泊——产生了炉渣。 随后，第 5 集的提示指示智能体永远不要尝试二级或三级融合，从而排除了它尚未测试的组合。 这个案例表明，经过处理的提示如何能够超越已观察到的失败情况而进行泛化。 但它并未证明压缩是造成与 Memory 相比的累积差异的原因。

paragraphs.en: In Poisoner , OpenCode–GPT-5 Mini trial 3 (seed 2) serves dish 0 at all three banquets in episodes 2, 3, and 5, even though dishes at that position are both accepted and rejected. Its saved notes describe a policy of always serving the same index. By contrast, OpenCode–Kimi K3 trial 1 (seed 2) compares accepted dishes across episodes 1 and 2 and identifies sourness as irrelevant. In episode 3, an accepted non-hot dish leads it to rule out temperature and then test saltiness. These cases use recorded actions and visible narration within the first five episodes. They illustrate different uses of feedback, not the frequency of either behavior across all trials.
paragraphs.zh: 在 Poisoner 中，OpenCode–GPT-5 Mini 试验 3（种子 2）在第 2、3 和 5 集的所有三场宴会中都供应了第 0 道菜，尽管该位置上的菜肴既被接受也被拒绝。 其保存的笔记描述了一项始终供应相同索引菜肴的策略。 相比之下，OpenCode–Kimi K3 试验 1（种子 2）则比较了第 1 集和第 2 集中被接受的菜肴，并判断酸味无关紧要。 在第 3 集中，一道被接受的非辛辣菜肴使其排除了温度的可能性，随后开始测试咸度。 这些案例在前五集内使用了记录下来的操作和可见的叙述。 它们展示了反馈的不同用途，而非所有试验中这两种行为出现的频率。

paragraphs.en: For each game, we select the Top-1, Top-3, and Top-5 players by their highest observed score within the scoring window. All records must have a completed first episode. If Max is tied, we prefer records with at least two scored episodes, then break remaining ties by the first episode attaining Max, Mean, LG, and LS. This tie-breaking rule supports analysis of learning while preserving the selected Max values.
paragraphs.zh: 对于每场比赛，我们根据评分窗口内观察到的最高分数，选出 Top-1、Top-3 和 Top-5 智能体。 所有记录都必须包含一个已完成的第一集。 如果 Max 值相同，我们优先选择至少有两个得分集的记录；若仍有并列，则按第一集达到 Max、Mean、LG 和 LS 的顺序进行破折。 这一破折规则既支持对学习过程的分析，又能保留所选的 Max 值。

paragraphs.en: Using a learned clue rather than probing again. In SynergyCorp with seed 2, trial 1, episode 10, three OpenCode agents start from the same game instance under a 30-action budget. Opus 5 uses a mapping learned in earlier episodes from visible desk traits to preferred actions, so it often selects an effective action immediately and scores 137. paragraphs.en: The savings differ by comparison. Memory supplies retained histories with each action request, giving it the largest input volume. EvoTest, Reflexion, ReasoningBank, and AWM generate additional updates between episodes. EvoTest’s updates alone use 11.5K generated tokens per episode, exceeding OpenCode’s total generation of 7.2K tokens. OpenCode uses fewer model calls: one GemForge trace batches nine game actions into a single call and returns only the last 60 output lines. Under the pricing snapshot, Kimi K3 generation costs $15 per million tokens versus $3 for fresh input, yielding generation costs of $0.108 for OpenCode, $0.369 for EvoTest, and $0.184 for ReasoningBank per episode. Reflexion and AWM have lower total estimated costs than OpenCode, alongside lower Max scores.
paragraphs.zh: 这些节省量在比较时存在差异。 内存供应为每次动作请求保留了历史记录，从而使其输入规模最大。 EvoTest、Reflexion、ReasoningBank 和 AWM 会在不同回合之间生成额外的更新。 仅 EvoTest 的更新每回合就使用了 11.5K 个生成的标记，超过了 OpenCode 总共 7.2K 个标记的生成量。 OpenCode 使用的模型调用次数更少：一次 GemForge 追踪将九个游戏动作合并为单次调用，并且仅返回最后 60 行输出。 根据当前的定价快照，Kimi K3 的生成成本为每百万标记 15 美元，而新输入的成本为 3 美元，因此 OpenCode、EvoTest 和 ReasoningBank 每回合的生成成本分别为 0.108 美元、0.369 美元和 0.184 美元。 Reflexion 和 AWM 的总估算成本低于 OpenCode，但它们的 Max 分数也更低。

paragraphs.en: Scope of the rule annotations. The labels provide supplementary qualitative evidence from interaction records. They do not measure rule discovery within the scoring window. The first five games use complete-rule criteria. Criteria for the other games also include successful execution supported by observed performance. Terse logs, especially for GPT-5.6-SOL, can leave a target unverified even when a successful policy uses it.
paragraphs.zh: 规则标注的范围。 这些标签提供了来自交互记录的补充性定性证据。 它们不衡量评分窗口内的规则发现情况。 前五局游戏使用完整规则标准。 其他游戏的标准还包括由观察到的表现所支持的成功执行。 简略的日志，尤其是 GPT-5.6-SOL 的日志，即使策略成功使用了目标，也可能导致该目标未被验证。
